action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (on-device deployment rationale, target hardware, success metrics), pain points (current workflow friction, performance concerns, compatibility risks), and acceptance criteria (performance thresholds, ease-of-adoption, fallback strategies) for the transformer model export and ExecuTorch lowering workflow.

Interview questions designed to elicit user goals (on-device transformer deployment workflow), pain points (export/lowering complexity, performance uncertainty), and acceptance criteria (latency, memory, ease-of-use) using 5W1H and Socratic techniques. Questions decompose the requirement into user context, technical constraints, performance expectations, and validation methods to ground subsequent requirement modeling.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit end-user goals (on-device deployment targets), pain points (export/lowering friction, performance bottlenecks), and acceptance criteria (metrics, reference implementations, supported architectures). Questions decompose the e2e workflow into critical decision points: model selection, StaticCache integration, export constraints, ExecuTorch delegation, and performance validation. Chain-of-Thought reasoning identifies that 'reasonable performance' and workflow automation are under-specified and require clarification before requirements modeling.

End-users need a unified on-device transformer deployment workflow that seamlessly integrates StaticCache across HuggingFace loading, PyTorch export, and ExecuTorch lowering stages, delivering reasonable performance guarantees out-of-the-box to eliminate manual optimization barriers and accelerate on-device inference adoption.

End-users require streamlined e2e on-device transformer deployment eliminating manual optimization steps across tools, with StaticCache automatically managed through export-to-lowering pipeline and ExecuTorch delegates providing out-of-the-box performance guarantees, reducing expertise barriers and deployment friction.

End users require a unified e2e workflow eliminating manual optimization friction across HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline, with persistent StaticCache configuration and out-of-the-box performance guarantees to reduce deployment cycles from weeks to days while lowering expertise barriers for non-specialist teams.

Clarifying target model architectures, performance metrics, StaticCache behavior across pipeline stages, delegate selection criteria, expected user expertise, failure mode handling, validation mechanisms, and quantization integration to fully scope the e2e on-device transformer workflow.

Six clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities in transformer export workflow: quantify 'reasonable performance' metrics, specify supported model architectures, clarify StaticCache consistency across pipeline stages, define delegate auto-selection behavior, establish compatibility validation timing, and confirm device target scope.

EndUser raises 5 clarification questions targeting ambiguous success metrics ('reasonable performance'), model scope boundaries, StaticCache configuration consistency across pipeline stages, delegate selection logic, and performance regression thresholds. These questions directly address pain points around expertise barriers and performance guarantee gaps in the current transformer deployment workflow.

End-user requirements are validated with strong business justification. Three refinements needed: (1) quantify performance targets with explicit metrics across device classes, (2) prioritize model scope (BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B), (3) document StaticCache configuration behavior across pipeline stages. Pain points and workflow automation expectations confirmed as requirements drivers.

End-user requirements validated and refined: e2e HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch workflow with StaticCache is confirmed critical. Refinements required: quantify 'reasonable performance' with explicit latency/memory/throughput targets per device class; prioritize BERT-base/GPT-2/Llama2-7B in Phase 1 with documented performance cliffs for larger models; clarify StaticCache configuration propagation across pipeline stages; provide automated guidance and profiling to reduce expertise barriers.

End-user requirements validated and refined: confirmed need for seamless HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline with StaticCache; quantified 'reasonable performance' with explicit latency/memory/throughput targets; prioritized Phase 1 model scope (BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B); clarified StaticCache configuration consistency requirements; established performance guarantee expectations to eliminate manual optimization barriers.

Consolidated 8 interview records from EndUser dialogue on transformers_2024q3 on-device workflow. Validated core requirement: seamless HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline with StaticCache and delegates. Identified 3 critical unresolved clarifications (performance metrics quantification, StaticCache immutability, architecture-specific bottlenecks) and 1 refined scope (Phase 1: BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B). All records follow ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability format with source attribution and resolution status.

Synthesized 8 hierarchical user requirements (4 MUST, 2 SHOULD, 1 COULD, 1 WON'T) for transformers_2024q3 on-device workflow. Core MUST requirements address end-to-end HuggingFace→ExecuTorch pipeline with StaticCache consistency, quantified performance guarantees (<100ms mobile latency, <500MB memory), and Phase 1 model prioritization (BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B). SHOULD requirements focus on expertise barrier elimination and automatic performance delegate application. All items traced to interview records, pain points, and user confirmations per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148.

Formulated 9 targeted deployer questions spanning infrastructure constraints (hardware topology, accelerator availability), security mandates (model encryption, data residency, compliance), scalability expectations (device heterogeneity, iteration cadence), and operational concerns (telemetry, configuration management, rollback safety) to bridge the gap between functional e2e workflow requirements and production deployment realities for the transformers_2024q3 on-device use-case.

Deployer dialogue targets three critical dimensions: (1) Infrastructure constraints—device classes, memory/compute limits, CI/CD integration, versioning strategy; (2) Security mandates—model IP protection, audit logging, compliance requirements; (3) Scalability expectations—concurrent deployment scale, multi-team architecture support, shared infrastructure dependencies. Questions also probe performance measurement baselines and StaticCache configuration mutability to align automation heuristics with deployment realities.

Formulated 10 targeted deployment-focused questions probing infrastructure constraints (device classes, deployment pipeline, hardware SoCs), security mandates (model signing, data governance, cache sensitivity), scalability expectations (model size variance, performance cliffs, memory constraints), and performance validation ownership. Questions apply 5W1H and Socratic techniques to clarify deployer responsibilities for performance guarantees, benchmarking infrastructure, and operational observability across the e2e HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch workflow.

Deployer constraints enforce <100ms mobile/<50ms edge latency SLAs, immutable StaticCache validation across pipeline stages, ARM/x86/accelerator delegate support with graceful CPU fallback, cost-optimized delegate selection per device class, and automated performance validation gates. Operational procedures mandate telemetry profiling, rollback safety, and pre-validated model recipes to eliminate expertise barriers and guarantee deployment-ready performance out-of-the-box for Phase 1 architectures (BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B).

Deployer response establishes infrastructure constraints (≤500MB mobile footprint, <100ms latency targets, ARM NEON/x86 SIMD support), security mandates (cryptographic StaticCache attestation, delegate code signing), scalability targets (BERT-base/GPT-2/Llama2-7B Phase 1 with automated device-class scaling), and operational procedures (automated cache reconciliation, delegate selection, benchmark validation) enabling end-to-end on-device transformer deployment without manual optimization expertise.

Deployer responds with 10 operationalized infrastructure constraints, security mandates, scalability targets, and cost-optimized operational procedures enabling automated transformer deployment via HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch pipeline with immutable StaticCache configuration, cryptographic attestation, device-aware delegate selection, and quantified performance SLAs (<100ms mobile, <50ms edge accelerators, <25ms cloud) across BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B Phase 1 scope.

Five operational clarifications required to operationalize infrastructure constraints and security mandates: (1) ExecuTorch delegate composition and coverage strategy for target device classes, (2) StaticCache cryptographic attestation enforcement mechanism and cache-drift recovery procedures, (3) performance target validation methodology and baseline device specifications, (4) availability-cost-performance trade-off strategy for on-device→cloud fallback, (5) Phase 1 model scope precision including quantization variants and sequence-length constraints. These clarifications align with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 deploy environment checklist requirements and resolve ambiguities between performance guarantees (UR-003) and technical constraints (IC-001/IC-002).

Deployer raises 6 clarification questions addressing critical gaps in operational execution: (1) ExecuTorch delegate coverage strategy and fallback behavior; (2) StaticCache cryptographic attestation mechanism and drift recovery; (3) Performance target validation operationalization (per-token vs. per-inference, batch assumptions); (4) Deployment-readiness gate criteria beyond metrics; (5) StaticCache configuration immutability semantics across pipeline stages; (6) Phase 1 scope boundary and performance cliff documentation. Chain-of-thought: Infrastructure constraints (IC-001/002) and security mandates (SM-001) lack operational detail required for implementation. Clarifications must resolve before deployment architecture can be finalized. Recommend stakeholder alignment on delegate strategy, cache attestation workflow, and performance validation methodology.

Deployer requires 5 clarifications on StaticCache cryptographic attestation mechanics (validation frequency, key management, failure handling), ExecuTorch delegate selection automation (capability detection, fallback strategy), performance target operationalization (measurement methodology, SLA enforcement, cost-performance trade-offs), automatic cache reconciliation logic (parameter prioritization, conflict resolution), and Phase 1 model scope with documented performance cliffs. Chain-of-thought reasoning identifies gaps between security mandates (SM-001), infrastructure constraints (IC-001/IC-002), and automation requirements (UR-002/UR-006) that require explicit operational decision criteria to enable end-to-end workflow deployment.

Deployer validation confirms UR-001 through UR-004 MUST requirements are deployment-ready pending infrastructure constraint operationalization (delegate coverage, device baselines, benchmark methodology). UR-005/UR-006 SHOULD requirements require clarification on automation scope and delegate minimum viable set. Critical refinements needed: SM-001 cryptographic attestation mechanism, IC-002 performance validation strategy with device baselines and percentile latency acceptance criteria, and delegate auto-selection logic for device class targeting. Recommend Phase 1 release with core e2e workflow functional, baseline performance validation, and cache immutability enforcement; secondary targets (Llama2-13B+) deferred to Phase 2.

Phase 1 scope (BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B) confirmed; Phase 2 defers larger variants pending optimization validation.

Operating environment specification for transformers_2024q3 captures on-device deployment prerequisites: ARM/x86 processors with optional accelerators (NPU/GPU), strict memory ceilings (500–1200MB), latency targets (<100ms mobile, <50ms edge accelerators), offline-first network model, cryptographically-attested StaticCache immutability across load→export→lower pipeline, Phase 1 architecture support (BERT-base, GPT-2, Llama2-7B), and deterministic benchmark validation framework enabling zero-shot deployment without manual optimization.
